summary: Wallowa County, OR summit: a 1934 timber tower fell in 1940; a 1941 steel Aermotor was removed in the 1950s; the ground cabin is reported still on the summit.

facts.design: 100' treated timber tower with L-6 cab (1934); 101' steel Aermotor tower (1941)
facts.status_note: Both towers are gone: the 1934 timber tower fell in 1940, and the 1941 steel tower was removed in the 1950s (no source gives an exact year). The ground cabin (living quarters) is reported to remain on the summit, with no source describing its condition now

access.note: Wallowa-Whitman National Forest land; no source read says whether the summit is open to visitors or how to reach it

corrections.why: Both sources say the 1934 tower fell down in the wind in 1940. The tower that was removed, in the 1950s, is the 1941 steel Aermotor that replaced it.

corrections.proposed: 100' treated timber tower with L-6 cab (1934); later 101' steel Aermotor tower (1941)
corrections.why: Aermotor describes only the 1941 replacement. The site's first tower was treated timber with an L-6 cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief lists firelookout.com as 'standing'. The page we read is headed 'R.I.P. 1934-1940' and describes the tower as fallen. No source we read says a tower stands on the site.
The register says the ground cabin is still on the summit; Forest Lookouts says the living quarters remain on site. Both agree the cabin is there, but neither gives a date or condition.

notes_for_editor: The brief's record has two errors, both corrected above: the 1940 event is a fall, not a removal, and the design field names only the 1941 replacement. The brief's conflict note says firelookout.com shows 'standing'; the page we read shows 'R.I.P. 1934-1940', so the 'standing' value may come from another part of that site or be an error. Not checked further. The removal of the 1941 steel tower is recorded only as 'the 1950s' in both sources, so no removal event with a year is kept; the 1950 placeholder was removed on the 2026-10-09 fact-check. The staffing list comes from firelookout.com and is not complete; the story names only the first, the 1943 item, and the last. No photo URLs were found, so none are listed.
